device.description: Quad 16-bit voltage-output DAC (external VREFH/VREFL reference) with 24-bit SPI write-only interface, ENABLE, LDAC, RST with zero/mid-scale select (RSTSEL)
device.note: dac8555.pdf (SLAS475B) p.3 power requirements (AVDD 2.7-5.5 V, IOVDD 1.8-5.5 V), logic levels vs IOVDD, p.4 pin configuration and descriptions, p.5 serial write operation and timing, p.15 asynchronous clear (RST/RSTSEL) and input shift register (Figure 47), p.16 load commands, power-down modes (Table 1), control matrix (Table 2), p.17 SYNC interrupt and power-on reset to zero-scale/midscale, p.18 power-down modes, p.21 LDAC and ENABLE pin

protocol.note: 24-bit word: DB23-DB22 0 0, LD1 LD0 (DB21-DB20), DB19 don't care, DAC select (DB18-DB17), PD0 (DB16), DB15-DB0 data (or PD1 PD2 in DB15-DB14 when PD0 = 1). Decoded at the 24th SCLK falling edge; SYNC rising earlier discards the word

pages: p.3 (supplies, logic inputs), p.4 (pins), p.5 (timing), p.15 (RST, input shift register Figure 47), p.16 (Tables 1-2), p.17 (SYNC interrupt, power-on reset), p.18 (power-down), p.21 (LDAC, ENABLE)
notModeled: analog outputs and output buffers (VOUTx never driven); power-down output loads stored in PWR only

the power-down condition is data in the buffer (TR/DR bits 17-16) and takes effect when the buffer is loaded; the model stores it per channel in PWR at once and clears it on the next data word to that channel. Loads of a power-down word (LD = 01, broadcast) do not change the DAC data register; LD = 10 loads all DAC registers from the buffers
ENABLE high: the device ignores the serial port; modeled by gating every command on the ENABLE level (STRAP.EN)
LDAC is a rising-edge trigger; synchronous updates use the LD1:LD0 load commands (LDAC tied low)
no read-back: the interface is write-only
IOVDD 1.8-2.7 V is allowed with degraded timing; vcc uses the 1.8-5.5 V IOVDD range of the power requirements table
SCLK limits (50 / 25 MHz) and setup/hold times

RSTSEL selects zero-scale reset with straight binary coding (low) or mid-scale reset with two's complement coding (high); the stored code after reset is 0 in both cases, so the register reset is 0 and the coding is analog-only
DB23/DB22 must be 0 except in broadcast words
variants: dac8555.pdf covers only the DAC8555. DAC8554 is the same core with A0/A1 address pins in place of RST/RSTSEL; DAC8565 adds a 2.5-V internal reference.
